about: Baseline of the proof lint (ADR 0933, phase B; scripts/proof-lint.mjs): per file and kind, how many hits of a code shape that decides a silence without a fact stand and why. A hit not counted fails; a count that fell fails until `--update` lowers it. A `why` is a stated fact or `pending-review` (counted, frozen, not yet audited).

finding-filter.why: `rows.dedup()` over the sorted release triples (solid-js, signals, web) of the installation: equal triples are one release; the gap finding is built from the distinct rows, so nothing is dropped from a report

ADR 0696: a violation at a site the whole program proves unreached is dropped under DropPass::SiteUnreached (ProofStage, written to the proof log); an uncertifiable row is never dropped here, and a withheld one flips the status

the attribution seam itself (ADR 0958): SC80xx findings in a package are dropped under the typed premise PackageStyleNotProject, and supersede_claims drops a handed-value claim only where a violation of the same rule stands inside its span (SupersededByViolation); both are DropPass stages of the proof log

name-only-match.why: `this` is a reserved word (its text is the ThisExpression); `arguments` is a spelling used only to refuse a proof (the true branch returns None/false); `Reflect` and `Proxy` are matched only where `reference_declaration(..)` is none, so no binding shadows the global, or are refused when one exists
`this` is a reserved word: its source text identifies exactly the ThisExpression and no binding can shadow it, so the spelling is the syntax, not a name

finding-filter.why: `objects.retain` removes the walk-bound placeholder (an empty path) from the work list and the same branch pushes the site itself as a getter location, which stands for what was not walked: an obligation, no finding dropped

name-only-match.why: `value` is the prop key of a provider element whose tag `is_context_reference` resolved to a context exactly; a tag that is not one exact identifier marks the census unkeyed, so no provider census closes

finding-filter.why: incremental resolver state (bindings, census, unkeyed ids) pruned to the ids the current file order still ranks: the entries of files that left the project; no finding is held in it
SC9012 dispatch obligations of a closed-program export are discharged under the typed premise ClosedProgramExportDischarge (RowStage, ADR 0933) and listed in `discharged` for the proof log

name-only-match.why: `keyed` and `when` are the prop names of an element already resolved to the dialect's `Show` (`known_primitive(..) == Some(Show)`, never a lookalike); `arguments` is a spelling used only to refuse a proof (the true branch returns false)

a spelled runtime or standard name tied to an exact fact, or one that only adds hazards: `preload` is `lazy()`'s own method on an object `ReturnedUses` resolves to the exact symbols holding the factory's result (the span adds a use, never removes one); `prototype` picks the standard-root patch, resolved by `file.standard_root` (otherwise `UnownedPrototype`, owned by `PrototypeOwnerAt`); `Symbol.for` is the global `Symbol` (no declaration) and a non-computed member; a bare `Reflect` mention and a `require` call the facts did not record as a load only add the `Unknown` and `UnmodeledRequire` hazards

finding-filter.why: the sorted hazard site locations of one hazard id, deduplicated: an equal location is one site

silent-unmatched-slot.why: ADR 0950, feature `what-if` only: `hazard_of_id` answers none for an id that names no hazard of the table, and its one caller (what_if.rs) refuses the `--assume` argument with an error, so an unknown name is never an assumption; a default build does not compile it

default-on-missing.why: incremental-engine bookkeeping: a missing previous order, position or reader means 'recompute' or 'treat as changed' or 'append to an empty list', never a verdict about reactivity
incremental-engine bookkeeping: a missing previous order, position or reader means 'recompute' or 'treat as changed' or 'append to an empty list', never a verdict about reactivity

finding-filter.why: per-file contributions with no entries are dropped from the fold: a file with no rows contributes none

finding-filter.why: memo table bookkeeping: entries not live in the epoch, the keys of dropped entries and the readers a re-run lost are removed from the tables; no finding is held in them

name-only-match.why: `this` is a reserved word: its source text identifies exactly the ThisExpression and no binding can shadow it, so the spelling is the syntax, not a name

`effect` is the key of the bundle object a classified effect primitive takes (`v2_effect_function_status(.., slot, ..)` is asked of the primitive's own argument slot): a dialect-defined option key of a resolved call, not an identification of what the call is

finding-filter.why: two caches pruned to the current file paths; the SC6001 rows (directive_creations) are kept only for a proven apply and the drop is the logged stage ApplyExecution::NotProven (an unknown apply drops the row: a review item of ADR 0958, the rule is partly silent); `retain_recording` names each row it removes as SiteSilence::ApplyNeverRuns with its premise (ADR 0936)

default-on-missing.why: loop control of a `retain`: a candidate no arm joins yet (`None`) is kept undecided for the next round, so the default keeps a candidate open and decides nothing silent

finding-filter.why: `undecided.retain` is the fixed point's work list of candidate paths: a candidate that joins an arm moves to `grown`; none is a finding

default-on-missing.why: `within` is an optional filter of which compiler facts may place the span: `None` means the caller asked for no restriction, which is the question `execution_role_where` is asked without it, not a verdict

untagged-silent-role.why: four candidate (span, role, rank) tuples of execution_role_where's compiler regions: none is an answer; the chosen candidate is returned through role_arm! as execution_role.execution_role_where.compiler-region

name-only-match.why: `eval` is a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof (a direct eval can reach any local binding without an identifier use): the true branch returns false/None/the unchanged slot, so a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

untagged-silent-role.why: none produces an answer: two are the expected-role arguments of named_helper_runs_during_body and one is a match pattern in excluded_role_holds

name-only-match.why: `prototype` only adds a refusal (`class_exposed` vetoes the proof); `value` is the provider's prop key beside `is_context_reference`, checked in both dialect branches (`context_provider_value_role`)

`children` is a prop name used only to REFUSE (a `children` attribute disqualifies the proof), inside a conjunction that also requires the element to resolve exactly to a primitive that renders its children through a callback (`exact_jsx_primitive_name`)

`children` is a prop name used only to REFUSE: a component's sole child expression is its `children` prop, and a `children` attribute competes with it, so the true branch refuses the flow (the comment at the site says both refuse)

default-on-missing.why: `call_in_jsx_expression`: with no owning function (module scope) any JSX around the call counts, the answer that ends a climb; `call_may_run_code`: a call that resolves to no primitive may run code, the answer that makes a claim uncertifiable. Neither answer extends a claim.

primitive-name-match.why: `supplied_owner` asks whether the call that is the owner argument, or the initializer of the `const` that is, is `getOwner()`: the one primitive whose value is the owner `runWithOwner` takes, so the question names that call, not a class of calls that behave alike.

default-on-missing.why: `walk_step`: with no bounded walk open (`None`) there is no bound to exceed, so the step is allowed; the step counter never produces a role or a verdict

finding-filter.why: `findings.dedup()` after the total ordering removes only a finding equal in every field (id, rule, kind, message, location, evidence) to its neighbour: the same row twice

name-only-match.why: a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof: reading `arguments` or `this` makes the function's parameters or receiver possibly aliased, so the true branch returns None/false and a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

finding-filter.why: ADR 0322: a call whose export is redirected is filed under the redirected symbol's key and removed from the one the index filed it under (an index of calls, no finding)

name-only-match.why: `component` only takes the value out of `used_as_render_value`: the reference then stays unaccounted unless the dialect's renderer resolves it (ADR 0138), and a project component's `component` prop is just a prop

`eval` is a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof (a direct eval can reach any local binding without an identifier use): the true branch returns false/None/the unchanged slot, so a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

`Object.assign` is a prefilter on the callee's text; both sites then require the call to be in `assign_builtin_calls`, which asks `mutation_builtin` (a Type Facts resolution to the built-in) before the call is treated as the built-in

`markRaw` is a presence veto (any mention makes store values possibly raw, the conservative answer); `createElement` is accepted only on a receiver `global_dom_variable` proves to be `document`; `addEventListener` is matched only as a bare identifier with `reference_declaration(..).is_none()` (the global) that is not a member property

finding-filter.why: the flush census's site list sorted and deduplicated: an equal (path, span) is one site
the locations of reads before their binding is initialized, sorted and deduplicated: an equal location is one site

name-only-match.why: a bare `Reflect` only widens `objects_may_be_assigned_into` (`true` is "some code may copy keys into an object"), the answer the member proofs treat as the veto; it never narrows it

`.length` is accepted as a primitive only on a receiver whose value origin is proven a built-in (`ValueOrigin::Builtin`) and only where the project never reassigns `length` on built-ins (`member_may_be_reassigned_on_builtin`), so the spelling is combined with a proof of the receiver

finding-filter.why: retained caches pruned to the current files and sources; `extract_if` splits the transported calls into the writers and the rest (a partition, nothing lost); `transported_calls.retain` (ADR 0299) removes the call target of an escaped or uninitialized literal, a proof withdrawn so the call is unproven, never a finding
the retained per-file state pruned to the current paths; `added.retain` removes owners with no added members from the propagation map

name-only-match.why: `eval` is a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof (a direct eval can reach any local binding without an identifier use): the true branch returns false/None/the unchanged slot, so a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative; `null` is a reserved literal, its source text identifies exactly the null literal

finding-filter.why: the log of reads one transport computation recorded, sorted and deduplicated: an equal read is one entry
the retained chunk cache keeps only the paths held exactly once in the current files; a dropped chunk is computed again

default-on-missing.why: a registered listener that is not a function literal and resolves to no function (`None`) is assumed to reach project code, which makes the registration a defect (the module's veto): the default adds an obligation, never a clean

name-only-match.why: a spelled `addEventListener` registration only produces an uncertain `ReactiveDispatchUnresolved` obligation (`push`) or widens `project_reaches`, the listener-reach premise a veto reads; it is never a proof or a violation

`on` and `children` are the prop names of a boundary the code has already resolved: every element and call reaches them only through `known_primitive(&primitives.jsx[index])` or `primitives.calls[index]` with `boundary_on_may_hold_outside`, so the spelling is the primitive's own prop, not an identification of what the element is; the candidate log of batch-11 slice 0 (`log_candidates`, measurement only) reads the same two props through the same resolved boundary (`known_primitive` / `primitives.calls[index]`)

finding-filter.why: three retained caches (file chunks, dependency states, prop sources) pruned to the current paths and symbols; a dropped entry is computed again

name-only-match.why: `this` is a reserved word: its source text identifies exactly the ThisExpression and no binding can shadow it, so the spelling is the syntax, not a name; `arguments` is a spelling used only to refuse a proof (the true branch returns None/false), so a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof: reading `arguments` or `this` makes the function's parameters or receiver possibly aliased, so the true branch returns None/false and a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative
`Object.freeze`: the receiver spelled `Object` is refused when `reference_declaration(receiver)` is some, so a shadowing binding is excluded and the global is what remains

a spelled prop key beside an exact fact, never a binding: a JSX attribute name (`when`, `fallback`, `each`, `value`, `ref`) is tested only where the element resolves exactly (`element_primitive`, `jsx_primitive_name`, or the holder's `reference_declaration` is the context declaration) or as a refusal (`!= Some("ref")`, `!= Some("value")`); `children` covers only where `is_props_of` resolves the member's object to the component's props parameter or an exact `const` alias (the foreign-object false clean, ADR 0668), and its second use only answers `Unresolved`
`default` is the key the dialect's `lazy` reads from the loader's module (`renders_loaded_default_argument` for the exact primitive at the call); an own `then` is a spelled refusal

finding-filter.why: callback-owner sites sorted by their order key and deduplicated: an equal site is one site
ADR 0713: an exported context a namespace or module load may reach leaves the candidates and becomes the verdict Open (`free.insert(.., Open)`), an obligation, in the same closure

name-only-match.why: `null` is a reserved literal; `undefined` is matched only where `reference_declaration(..).is_none()` (the global); `value` and `children` are prop names of a provider element the census has already resolved, and `children` is read off a member whose object `reference_declaration` binds to the wrapper's own props parameter

default-on-missing.why: pending-review for `fragment_child`'s; the other is `can_hand_itself_on`'s (ADR 0971, the re-review of #225, B1): no list of the producer's references of a function expression's own name answers yes, the function may hand itself on, which keeps the site's row: the answer that fails closed, never a silence

name-only-match.why: `bind` only follows a transport shape toward the object, whose primitive `referenced_primitive` resolves exactly first; the name describes the transport, never a primitive

text-premise.why: JSX grammar: a child of an element whose source starts with `{` is exactly an expression container, since a text child cannot contain an unescaped brace; this is a syntactic test of the node's own source, not a spelling match on a symbol

prose-hand-off.why: `action_step_leaf_owner` is a positive lookup: `Some(owner)` only where every caller of the action's first step has the leaf owner and no `yield` may come first; the `return None` states that no leaf owner is proven, and `containing_leaf_owner` then tries its other routes, so the comment's "not this read's claim" scopes a lookup and hands no case to another check

finding-filter.why: `apply_settled_gates`: an out-of-band `onSettled` (the fixed point's OutOfBand decision: no owner at the call, so the callback is a plain queued function) sheds its leaf operations and an unproven gate keeps them uncertain; a cleanup requirement written in a leaf's own callback whose gate is decided Owned is dropped because SC3001 owns the claim there (ADR 0942). Neither drop is a proof-log line yet (a review item of ADR 0958)
the owner graph's symbol index drops the entry of a node that changed (`entries.retain`): state maintenance, no finding

`rows.retain` selects the program rows located in a package for the entry table (a view, nothing removed from the program); the `dedup_by` calls remove a project site, or a claim of the same rule, equal in location to its neighbour in the table and in the handed-value claims, which keep one row per site and rule

default-on-missing.why: polarity: yes means the value may be a function, which keeps the site (an uncertifiable SC2002 row, never a silence); a symbol with no declaration the compiler resolved, or a list of none, is a value nothing says is a type, so it stays a site
an import binding with no entity, or whose symbol is undeclared, sets `source_module_unresolved`, which marks the row uncertain with a blocker: the default adds a blocker, never a clean

finding-filter.why: `reasons.retain` removes a reason (NotRenderEffect) from the list that accounts a read safe when the component's identity is uncertain: fewer reasons, so the claim is accounted less, never more

ADR 0933 `gate_rows!` drops the rows of a compiler-discarded region under the typed premise CompilerDiscardedRegion (RowStage, proof log); the index cache is pruned to the current paths; the SC4001 effect requirement of a JSX site is dropped where SC6002 proves the throw on every run (`jsx_phase_sites`, ADR 0883) and kept uncertain otherwise

name-only-match.why: `__proto__` is a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof (a `__proto__` attribute is lowered to an entry that installs a prototype on the props object; the true branch returns None): a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

finding-filter.why: ADR 0933 drop passes with typed premises written to the proof log: ExecutionPaths (a violation on a path no client run reaches), the unfollowed-dependency-value uncertainty where the value is proven, and SC1001 under a more specific rule at the same span (OwnedByEnabledRule)

default-on-missing.why: `nested` labels a candidate line of the dry-run log: yes (nested) when no innermost function is found; the label silences nothing and decides no finding (measurement only)

name-only-match.why: `sync` is the option name of the options object of a call already resolved to a primitive that supports it (`dialect.supports_sync_option(kind)`): the producer's own reading of the option, repeated for the candidate log (measurement only, decides no finding)

primitive-name-match.why: the dry-run candidate list of batch-11 slice 0 (measurement only: behind SOLID_CHECKER_IR_PROOF_CANDIDATES, written to the proof log, decides no finding) names the primitive each of SC2004 `resolve`, SC2005 `until` and SC2007 `dynamic` is about; `kind` is the dialect classification of an exactly resolved call, the first test the matching static_api.rs arm applies; the rule-owned universes of slice 8 replace this list, and the dialect names the primitive there

finding-filter.why: reachability caches pruned to the current paths and to the files recomputed; no finding is held in them

`writes.retain(replaced)` swaps a write for its transported version (the same location, kept once); the SC9012 `value-*` dispatch obligation is dropped where an uncaptured-source SC9012 stands at the same span (one obligation stays); a write or an async read whose declaration the producer withdrew is replaced by a named obligation (`held.push(obligation)`, fail closed)

name-only-match.why: `routes` is the option key of the config handed to the exact router `create` call (`locals.calls(.., &locals.create)`), in a closed `this`-free literal
a write of `apply` beside `useAction` only vetoes the proof (the function returns the reason it gives up)

default-on-missing.why: `None` (TypeScript does not resolve the member) sets `unresolved_member = true`, and the comment at the site says an unresolved member is uncertain, never a violation: the default answers yes to 'unproven'

name-only-match.why: `serializeArgs` is an option key of the exact `configureServerFunctionsClient` call (declaration name and origin module checked); options that are not a closed literal leave the proof `Unresolved`, and a closed one without the key is the `Disabled` proof

primitive-name-match.why: the three comparisons only choose the word `status` or `header` in a finding's message (wording of SC7005 after the dialect decided the call is an http-response primitive); whether a finding exists was decided before them

finding-filter.why: `premises.retain(at.is_some())`: a silence is recorded only with a premise that names a span; a premise with none is dropped and the site is not ended, so it stays an unaccounted uncertifiable row (ADR 0936)

name-only-match.why: `children` and `keyed` are prop keys read off an element the caller resolved to a dialect primitive: `children` only collects a candidate expression, and a `keyed` that no proven function decides is the ambiguous `DynamicFlag`, for which the dialect claims no accessor

finding-filter.why: the identity cache pruned to the current file paths; no finding is held in it
pass 9: a runtime source stays a source only while no file writes it; a written source is withdrawn, a proof removed (its readers become unproven), never a finding

name-only-match.why: `keyed` is the prop key of an element whose `jsx_primitive_name` is a known dialect primitive (`known_primitive`); the accessor parameters are the dialect's answer for that primitive and key form

a spelling used only to REFUSE a proof: reading `arguments` or `this` makes the function's parameters or receiver possibly aliased, so the true branch returns None/false and a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative

finding-filter.why: the tracker drops the computation's own file from the dependency list it hands to the enclosing computation: dependency bookkeeping, no finding

name-only-match.why: `sync` is the key of the options literal of a call whose primitive kind is already resolved and for which the dialect says the option exists (`supports_sync_option(kind)`, `options_argument(kind)`), not an identification of what the call is

default-on-missing.why: an import binding with no entity, or whose symbol is undeclared, is `unresolved` and yields the unresolved-import defect: the default adds an obligation, never a clean

finding-filter.why: the callback-pattern site spans sorted and deduplicated (`sites.dedup()`) before each is judged: an equal span is one site

prose-hand-off.why: SC1003's own claim (the bindings are read once and then never update) is the sentence; the `continue` rests on a positive compiler fact, `discarded_region_contains` (the compiler deleted the destructure), and not on another check's answer

finding-filter.why: `next.retain(!ahead.holds)` filters the next wave of the continuation walk to members not yet visited: a work list, no row

default-on-missing.why: a wrapper whose text is missing, or that mentions `arguments`, returns `open()` (unproven): the default refuses the proof

name-only-match.why: the identifier is spelled `Promise` and has no declaration in the file (`reference_declaration(..).is_none()`), so it names the global that a local or imported binding would shadow
`Promise` as a constructor callee and `undefined` are matched only where `reference_declaration(..)` is none, so no binding shadows the global; `null` is a literal keyword
`fallback` is read only off an element with `element_primitive == Errored` (`handled_above`)

finding-filter.why: `references.retain(non-empty)` removes a symbol with no reference locations from the reference map; no location is lost

name-only-match.why: `value` is the prop key of a provider of the exact context key the census resolved; anything else is `self.open()`

finding-filter.why: ported from eslint-plugin-solid (ADR 0919): the member-chain links at or inside the root expression are not past it; a link list of the walk, not rows

name-only-match.why: no silence is granted by the spelling: `.apply` only adds a call to `reactive_source_uncaptured`'s candidates (`hands_over_a_source`), whose callee is then resolved exactly (`caller_target`, `undescribed_callee`); `arguments` is the implicit binding (`reference_declaration` none) and a bare mention only keeps the parameter walk running; `keyed` and `each` are prop keys of an element `primitives.jsx` resolved to `For`; `class` on a lowercase-led tag only makes a position type-owned, which yields an uncertifiable blocker or the same silence the unrecognized position gets (`type_owned_position`, ADR 0830)

prose-hand-off.why: the comment scopes this rule's own claim (a write through a member chain rooted at a call lands on whatever the call returned); the `continue` follows `push_unproven_container_write`, which records that write as an obligation unless ADR 0720's row proves the call returns a store value, so nothing is dropped and no other check is named

name-only-match.why: `map` only selects the candidate of `prefer-for`; the preference needs the callee to resolve to a valid standard-library array or tuple `map` declaration, else nothing is reported

`this` is a reserved word: its source text identifies exactly the ThisExpression and no binding can shadow it, so the spelling is the syntax, not a name; `arguments` is a spelling used only to refuse a proof (the true branch returns None/false), so a miss or a shadowing declaration only makes the check more conservative
